summary: The tests compile and run without errors, correctly using Playwright APIs and asynchronous assertions. The testCaseIds are preserved in test titles, and all GENERATED tests are included. However, some selectors are weak or placeholders, and assumptions made in selectors and assertions reduce reliability. Iteration over element handles instead of Locator violates best practices and risks flakiness.

issues.description: In TC-003, the code uses page.$$(selector) to get an array of ElementHandle and then attempts to use expect(product).toBeClickable() on each handle. Playwright assertions should be applied on Locators, not ElementHandles. This violates best practices and risks flakiness or errors.
issues.recommendation: Use page.locator(selector) and iterate with locator.nth(i) or locator.first() for assertions instead of querying with page.$$.

issues.description: In all tests, selectors such as 'link with /product name/i', 'selector-for-related-products', and generic getByText or getByRole with minimal context are weak and rely on assumptions. This reduces test stability.
issues.recommendation: Use more specific selectors or data-testid attributes when possible to ensure stable and robust element targeting.

issues.description: In TC-001, URL validation only checks if the URL contains 'product-detail' which is weak to confirm the correct product detail page loaded.
issues.recommendation: Enhance validation by checking page content or more detailed URL structure to confirm that the expected product detail page was loaded.

recommendations: Replace page.$$ with page.locator to handle multiple elements properly.
Avoid using placeholder selectors like 'selector-for-related-products'; replace with real, stable selectors.
Improve URL and content validations in tests to strengthen assertion reliability.
Consider adding comments or test data management to reduce assumptions in selectors.
Refine selectors by using data attributes or unique identifiers instead of generic role or text queries.
